subject: Proposed City Charter Reform
overview: Hosts Danielle Balocca and Chelli Keshavan spoke with charter review committee member Milva McDonald about the upcoming ballot question to adopt a new city charter for Medford.

items.title: Podcast introduction and local restaurant favorites
items.summary: The hosts introduced the episode and shared their favorite local dining establishments.

items.title: Charter review process update
items.summary: Milva McDonald summarized the multi-year process of drafting the new charter, its approval as a home rule petition at the State House, and its placement on the upcoming municipal ballot.

items.title: Proposed structural changes to Medford government
items.summary: McDonald explained major structural reforms in the proposed charter, including transitioning the mayor to a four-year term with a four-term limit, creating a hybrid city council with ward representation, and allowing the school committee to elect its own chair.

items.title: Citizen participation and budgeting mechanisms
items.summary: The discussion outlined new provisions for group petitions, ballot initiatives, mayoral recall, and required early budget collaboration between the mayor, council, and school committee.

items.title: Public feedback and Ballot Question Committee advocacy
items.summary: The speakers addressed public feedback regarding the committee's appointment process and potential municipal costs, and highlighted resources available through the Medford Charter Now ballot question committee.
